content: Certainly. 1. Administer 1 gram of cefadroxil orally once daily or divided into two doses every 12 hours for a duration of 10 days. 2. For prophylaxis in dental or upper respiratory procedures, administer 2 grams of cefadroxil orally one hour before the procedure. 3. In cases of renal impairment: For creatinine clearance (CrCl) between 25-50 mL/min, administer every 12 hours. For CrCl between 10-25 mL/min, administer once daily. For CrCl less than 10 mL/min, administer every 36 hours. 4. For prophylaxis in pediatric patients undergoing dental or upper respiratory procedures, administer 50 mg/kg orally one hour before the procedure, not exceeding a total dose of 2 grams. 5. For pediatric infections, administer 30 mg/kg/day orally, divided into two doses every 12 hours, or as a single daily dose for 10 days, not exceeding 1 gram per dose. 6. Cefadroxil reduces the efficacy of live BCG vaccines due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Live bacterial vaccines should not be administered until antibiotic therapy is completed. 7. Avoid coadministration of cefadroxil with the cholera vaccine, as systemic antibiotics may inactivate the vaccine strain. Do not administer the cholera vaccine to patients who have received antibiotics within 14 days prior to vaccination. 8. Cefadroxil may reduce the efficacy of oral microbiota products containing bacterial spores. Complete antibiotic regimens 2-4 days before initiating oral microbiota therapy. 9. Cefadroxil decreases the efficacy of live typhoid vaccines due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Live bacterial vaccines should not be administered until antibiotic therapy is completed. 10. Cefadroxil increases the nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity of aminoglycosides such as amikacin, gentamicin, kanamycin, neomycin, streptomycin, and tobramycin. Use caution and monitor renal function closely. 11. Cefadroxil may interfere with the therapeutic effects of immune checkpoint inhibitors (e.g., atezolizumab, avelumab, balstilimab, camrelizumab, cemiplimab, dostarlimab, durvalumab, nivolumab, pembrolizumab, penpulimab, retifanlimab, sintilimab, tislelizumab, toripalimab). Use caution and monitor for reduced efficacy. 12. Cefadroxil may alter intestinal flora, reducing the efficacy of oral hormonal contraceptives (e.g., ethinyl estradiol, conjugated estrogens, estradiol, mestranol). While the risk of contraceptive failure is low, use caution and monitor. 13. Cefadroxil increases the toxicity of furosemide and voclosporin due to pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of nephrotoxicity. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 14. Cefadroxil increases the effects of warfarin, potentially altering coagulation. Use caution and monitor INR levels. 15. Cefadroxil increases the levels or effects of acidic (anionic) drugs such as aspirin, diclofenac, ibuprofen, indomethacin, ketoprofen, ketorolac, meloxicam, and others by competing for renal tubular clearance. The clinical significance is minor or unknown, but caution is advised. 16. Cefadroxil increases the levels or effects of certain diuretics (e.g., hydrochlorothiazide, indapamide, methyclothiazide) and NSAIDs (e.g., etodolac, fenoprofen, flurbiprofen) by competing for renal tubular clearance. The clinical significance is minor or unknown, but caution is advised. 17. Cefadroxil increases the levels or effects of ganciclovir and probenecid by competing for renal tubular clearance. Use caution and monitor. 18. Cefadroxil increases the levels or effects of mesalamine and balsalazide by competing for renal tubular clearance. The clinical significance is minor or unknown, but caution is advised. 19. Cefadroxil may reduce the efficacy of sodium picosulfate/magnesium oxide/anhydrous citric acid by altering colonic bacterial flora required for drug activation. Use caution and monitor. 20. Cefadroxil increases the levels or effects of temocillin and aztreonam due to pharmacodynamic synergism. This combination may be used synergistically against Enterobacteriaceae, but caution is advised. 21. Chloramphenicol reduces the efficacy of cefadroxil due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. The clinical significance is minor or unknown, but caution is advised.
